q: Fossil fuels consist of coal, petroleum and ______.
e: Fossil fuels consist of coal, petroleum and natural gas. Fossil fuels are coal, petroleum, and natural gas, formed from ancient remains and finite. Hydrogen would fill a different blank than natural gas.

q: Coal is fossilised plant material containing mainly carbon together with hydrogen, nitrogen and ______.
e: Coal is fossilised plant material containing mainly carbon together with hydrogen, nitrogen and sulphur. Sulphur is the idea that completes this fact. Chlorine would fill a different blank than sulphur.

q: Crude oil and natural gas were formed from the remains of dead animals and plants that lived in the ______.
e: Crude oil and natural gas were formed from the remains of dead animals and plants that lived in the seas. Seas is the idea that completes this fact. Forests would fill a different blank than seas.

q: Natural gas consists mainly of ______.
e: Natural gas consists mainly of methane, CH4. Methane, CH4 is the idea that completes this fact. Propane, C3H8 would fill a different blank than methane, CH4.

q: When coal is strongly heated in the absence of air, it produces a solid called ______.
e: When coal is strongly heated in the absence of air, it produces a solid called coke. Coke is the idea that completes this fact. Ash would fill a different blank than coke.

q: The main use of coke is as a ______ in the blast furnace for making iron.
e: The main use of coke is as a reducing agent in the blast furnace for making iron. Reducing agent is the idea that completes this fact. Oxidising agent would fill a different blank than reducing agent.

q: Crude oil is a mixture of many different ______ molecules.
e: Crude oil is a mixture of many different hydrocarbon molecules. A hydrocarbon contains only hydrogen and carbon. Carbohydrate would fill a different blank than hydrocarbon.

q: Non-renewable fuels are fuels which take millions of years to form and which are used up at a ______ rate.
e: Non-renewable fuels are fuels which take millions of years to form and which are used up at a rapid rate. Rapid is the idea that completes this fact. Slow would fill a different blank than rapid.

q: Renewable fuels are fuels produced from renewable resources such as ______.
e: Renewable fuels are fuels produced from renewable resources such as vegetable oils, animal oils, etc.. Vegetable oils, animal oils, etc. is the idea that completes this fact. Coal, oil, and gas would fill a different blank than vegetable oils, animal oils, etc.

q: Combustion of coal releases nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, particulate matter (PM), mercury and dozens of other substances known to be hazardous to ______.
e: Combustion of coal releases nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, particulate matter (PM), mercury and dozens of other substances known to be hazardous to human health. Human health is the idea that completes this fact. Soil fertility would fill a different blank than human health.

q: Myanmar has coal deposits in Shan State, Kachin State, Taninthayi Region and ______.
e: Myanmar has coal deposits in Shan State, Kachin State, Taninthayi Region and Sagaing Region. Sagaing Region is the idea that completes this fact. Bago Region would fill a different blank than Sagaing Region.

q: British Burma exported its first barrel of crude oil in ______.
e: British Burma exported its first barrel of crude oil in 1853. 1853 is the idea that completes this fact. 1887 would fill a different blank than 1853.

q: The London-based Burma Oil Company (BOC) began production in the Yenangyaung oil field in ______.
e: The London-based Burma Oil Company (BOC) began production in the Yenangyaung oil field in 1887. 1887 is the idea that completes this fact. 1853 would fill a different blank than 1887.

q: Most coal was formed during the ______ period (286–360 million years ago).
e: Most coal was formed during the Carboniferous period (286–360 million years ago). Carboniferous is the idea that completes this fact. Permian would fill a different blank than Carboniferous.

q: Coal contains between ______ carbon by mass.
e: Coal contains between 80 to 90% carbon by mass. 80 to 90% is the idea that completes this fact. 40 to 50% would fill a different blank than 80 to 90%.

q: Separation of crude oil takes place in a ______ into different fractions in an oil refinery.
e: Separation of crude oil takes place in a fractional distillation column into different fractions in an oil refinery. Distillation separates liquids by boiling point, then condenses the vapour. Combustion chamber would fill a different blank than fractional distillation column.

q: In fractional distillation, the fractions condense and come out of the column at different heights depending on their ______.
e: In fractional distillation, the fractions condense and come out of the column at different heights depending on their boiling points. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point. Densities would fill a different blank than boiling points.

q: The petroleum gas fraction comes out first at the top of the column because its molecules have the ______.
e: The petroleum gas fraction comes out first at the top of the column because its molecules have the lowest boiling points. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point. Greatest density would fill a different blank than lowest boiling points.

q: The residue at the bottom of the fractional distillation column is used to make bitumen for ______.
e: The residue at the bottom of the fractional distillation column is used to make bitumen for surfacing roads. Surfacing roads is the idea that completes this fact. Plastic bottles would fill a different blank than surfacing roads.

q: All the fractions from crude oil distillation are insoluble in water and ______ in air.
e: All the fractions from crude oil distillation are insoluble in water and burn in air. Burn is the idea that completes this fact. Dissolve would fill a different blank than burn.

q: Petrol (gasoline) has an approximate boiling point range of ______ °C.
e: Petrol (gasoline) has an approximate boiling point range of 35~75 °C. 35~75 is the idea that completes this fact. 500~600 would fill a different blank than 35~75.

q: Kerosene (paraffin) is used as a fuel for ______.
e: Kerosene (paraffin) is used as a fuel for jet aircraft. Jet aircraft is the idea that completes this fact. Space rockets would fill a different blank than jet aircraft.

q: Lubricating oil contains approximately ______ carbon atoms per molecule.
e: Lubricating oil contains approximately 19~35 carbon atoms per molecule. 19~35 is the idea that completes this fact. 1~4 would fill a different blank than 19~35.

q: Fuel oil is used as a fuel for ships, factories and ______.
e: Fuel oil is used as a fuel for ships, factories and central heating systems. Central heating systems is the idea that completes this fact. Laboratory burners would fill a different blank than central heating systems.

q: Refinery gas is used as bottled gas for gas cookers and ______.
e: Refinery gas is used as bottled gas for gas cookers and motor cars. Motor cars is the idea that completes this fact. Electric stoves would fill a different blank than motor cars.

q: Naphtha is primarily used to make ______.
e: Naphtha is primarily used to make petrochemicals. Petrochemicals is the idea that completes this fact. Fertilisers would fill a different blank than petrochemicals.

q: Diesel oil has an approximate boiling point range of ______ °C.
e: Diesel oil has an approximate boiling point range of 250~340 °C. 250~340 is the idea that completes this fact. 35~75 would fill a different blank than 250~340.

q: Bitumen is a black substance used to make surface roads and ______.
e: Bitumen is a black substance used to make surface roads and roofing. Roofing is the idea that completes this fact. Synthetic rubber would fill a different blank than roofing.

q: The fraction with the smallest molecules is ______.
e: The fraction with the smallest molecules is refinery gas. Refinery gas is the idea that completes this fact. Naphtha would fill a different blank than refinery gas.

q: The most viscous fraction from crude oil distillation is ______.
e: The most viscous fraction from crude oil distillation is bitumen. Bitumen is the idea that completes this fact. Diesel oil would fill a different blank than bitumen.

q: Cracking is a thermal decomposition process in which large alkane hydrocarbon molecules are broken down by passing them over a heated ______ under pressure.
e: Cracking is a thermal decomposition process in which large alkane hydrocarbon molecules are broken down by passing them over a heated catalyst under pressure. Catalyst is the idea that completes this fact. Filter would fill a different blank than catalyst.

q: When a catalyst is used in cracking, the process is called ______.
e: When a catalyst is used in cracking, the process is called catalytic cracking. Catalytic cracking breaks long hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful ones. Thermal distillation would fill a different blank than catalytic cracking.

q: The products of catalytic cracking are smaller alkanes used for fuels and ______ which are used to make polymers.
e: The products of catalytic cracking are smaller alkanes used for fuels and alkenes which are used to make polymers. Alkenes is the idea that completes this fact. Aromatics would fill a different blank than alkenes.

q: Cracking typically occurs at a temperature around ______.
e: Cracking typically occurs at a temperature around 500℃. 500℃ is the idea that completes this fact. 200℃ would fill a different blank than 500℃.

q: Common catalysts used in cracking include powdered minerals such as silica, alumina and ______.
e: Common catalysts used in cracking include powdered minerals such as silica, alumina and zeolites. Zeolites is the idea that completes this fact. Graphite would fill a different blank than zeolites.

q: The octane number of a fuel is determined by comparing its knocking behavior to a mixture of iso-octane (octane number 100) and ______ (octane number 0).
e: The octane number of a fuel is determined by comparing its knocking behavior to a mixture of iso-octane (octane number 100) and heptane (octane number 0). Heptane is the idea that completes this fact. Hexane would fill a different blank than heptane.

q: Branched-chain alkanes produced by cracking have ______ than unbranched alkanes.
e: Branched-chain alkanes produced by cracking have higher octane ratings than unbranched alkanes. Octane rating tells how well a petrol resists knocking in an engine. Lower boiling points would fill a different blank than higher octane ratings.

q: Ethene from cracking is used to prepare ethanol, polyethene, and ______.
e: Ethene from cracking is used to prepare ethanol, polyethene, and polychloroethene. Polychloroethene is the idea that completes this fact. Polypropene would fill a different blank than polychloroethene.

q: Propene polymerises to produce ______.
e: Propene polymerises to produce polypropene. Polypropene is the idea that completes this fact. Polyethene would fill a different blank than polypropene.

q: Thermal decomposition is the breaking down of a chemical compound caused by ______.
e: Thermal decomposition is the breaking down of a chemical compound caused by heat. Heat is the idea that completes this fact. Light would fill a different blank than heat.

q: A catalyst is a substance that speeds up the chemical reaction without getting ______.
e: A catalyst is a substance that speeds up the chemical reaction without getting consumed. Consumed is the idea that completes this fact. Dissolved would fill a different blank than consumed.

q: Engine knocking refers to the sharp sounds caused by combustion of some of the compressed air-fuel mixture in the ______.
e: Engine knocking refers to the sharp sounds caused by combustion of some of the compressed air-fuel mixture in the cylinder. Cylinder is the idea that completes this fact. Carburetor would fill a different blank than cylinder.

q: Cracking is important because there is greater demand for ______ than other fractions.
e: Cracking is important because there is greater demand for petrol and kerosene than other fractions. Petrol and kerosene is the idea that completes this fact. Refinery gas and naphtha would fill a different blank than petrol and kerosene.

q: Decane ($C_{10}H_{22}$) can crack to produce ethene and ______.
e: Decane (C10H22) can crack to produce ethene and 2,2,4-trimethyl pentane. 2,2,4-trimethyl pentane is the idea that completes this fact. Methane would fill a different blank than 2,2,4-trimethyl pentane.

q: Antiknocking agents such as tetraethyl lead are added to gasoline to increase the fuel's ______.
e: Antiknocking agents such as tetraethyl lead are added to gasoline to increase the fuel's octane rating. Octane rating tells how well a petrol resists knocking in an engine. Viscosity would fill a different blank than octane rating.

q: At the present rate of consumption, petroleum and natural gas may run out within ______.
e: At the present rate of consumption, petroleum and natural gas may run out within 50 years. 50 years is the idea that completes this fact. 250 years would fill a different blank than 50 years.

q: Coal will only last for a further ______ at current consumption rates.
e: Coal will only last for a further 250 years at current consumption rates. 250 years is the idea that completes this fact. 100 years would fill a different blank than 250 years.

q: An alternative fuel is an internal combustion engine fuel other than gasoline or ______.
e: An alternative fuel is an internal combustion engine fuel other than gasoline or diesel oil. Diesel oil is the idea that completes this fact. Kerosene would fill a different blank than diesel oil.

q: CNG stands for ______.
e: CNG stands for compressed natural gas. Compressed natural gas is the idea that completes this fact. Condensed nitrogen gas would fill a different blank than compressed natural gas.

q: LPG is composed of ______.
e: LPG is composed of propane and butane. Propane and butane is the idea that completes this fact. Ethanol and methanol would fill a different blank than propane and butane.

q: Biodiesel is made from plant oils or animal oils and consists of long-chain ______.
e: Biodiesel is made from plant oils or animal oils and consists of long-chain esters. Esters is the idea that completes this fact. Alcohols would fill a different blank than esters.

q: Biogas is produced from waste organic matter and consists mainly of ______.
e: Biogas is produced from waste organic matter and consists mainly of methane. Methane is the idea that completes this fact. Hydrogen would fill a different blank than methane.

q: Hydrogen fuel burns cleanly in air to produce ______, which is a non-pollutant.
e: Hydrogen fuel burns cleanly in air to produce steam, which is a non-pollutant. Steam is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon dioxide would fill a different blank than steam.

q: Most industrial hydrogen is manufactured from ______.
e: Most industrial hydrogen is manufactured from petrol and natural gas. Petrol and natural gas is the idea that completes this fact. Coal gasification would fill a different blank than petrol and natural gas.

q: In the production of hydrogen from methane, steam is passed over a ______ catalyst.
e: In the production of hydrogen from methane, steam is passed over a nickel catalyst. Nickel is the idea that completes this fact. Iron would fill a different blank than nickel.

q: Gasohol is a blended fuel made from petrol and ______.
e: Gasohol is a blended fuel made from petrol and ethanol. Ethanol is the idea that completes this fact. Biodiesel would fill a different blank than ethanol.

q: Transesterification involves treating seed oil with a basic catalyst such as ______.
e: Transesterification involves treating seed oil with a basic catalyst such as sodium hydroxide. Sodium hydroxide is the idea that completes this fact. Nickel would fill a different blank than sodium hydroxide.

q: The transesterification reaction produces biodiesel and ______.
e: The transesterification reaction produces biodiesel and glycerol. Glycerol is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon dioxide would fill a different blank than glycerol.

q: Hydrogen produces at least ______ as much heat energy per gram when burnt than any other common fuel.
e: Hydrogen produces at least twice as much heat energy per gram when burnt than any other common fuel. Twice is the idea that completes this fact. The same would fill a different blank than twice.

q: Natural gas offshore projects in Myanmar include the Yadana, Yetagun, Shwe Platform and ______ projects.
e: Natural gas offshore projects in Myanmar include the Yadana, Yetagun, Shwe Platform and Zawtika projects. Zawtika is the idea that completes this fact. Chauk would fill a different blank than Zawtika.

q: Biogas production leaves a solid residue that is used as a ______.
e: Biogas production leaves a solid residue that is used as a fertiliser. Fertiliser is the idea that completes this fact. Fuel would fill a different blank than fertiliser.

q: Methane accumulates in ______, where it can cause explosions.
e: Methane accumulates in coal-mines, where it can cause explosions. Coal-mines is the idea that completes this fact. Power stations would fill a different blank than coal-mines.

q: Marsh gas, which bubbles up through stagnant water in swamps and paddy fields, is also ______.
e: Marsh gas, which bubbles up through stagnant water in swamps and paddy fields, is also methane. Methane is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon monoxide would fill a different blank than methane.

q: Biodiesel is a potential substitute for ______.
e: Biodiesel is a potential substitute for petro-diesel. Petro-diesel is the idea that completes this fact. Kerosene would fill a different blank than petro-diesel.

q: Smaller quantities of hydrogen are produced by the electrolysis of water containing ______.
e: Smaller quantities of hydrogen are produced by the electrolysis of water containing sulphuric acid. Sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact. Potassium hydroxide would fill a different blank than sulphuric acid.
